title.en: The dog who ate too much

text.en: A rich lady loved her little dog so much that she nearly made him ill. How did the vet help?

The story is by James Herriot, a veterinary surgeon. He tells of Tricki Woo, a small Pekingese dog owned by the wealthy Mrs Pumphrey.
Mrs Pumphrey pampered Tricki with too many rich foods and sweets, so he grew fat, lazy and breathless.
She called the doctor in a state of panic, thinking Tricki was very ill, and begged him to save the dog.
Herriot saw at once that Tricki was only overweight and lacked exercise. He decided the only way was to take Tricki away from her house.
He took Tricki to his own surgery, with Mrs Pumphrey and the staff weeping and throwing coats at the car.
At Herriot's place Tricki was put on a strict diet and played with other dogs, so he became lean and lively.
After a few days he went home healthy, and Mrs Pumphrey called it a triumph of surgery, though no surgery was done.
The story shows that love without sense can harm a pet, and that good care means the right food and exercise.

problem.en: Tricki weighed 9 kg and lost 2 kg. What is his new weight?

text.en: Subtract the loss from the weight.

prompt.en: Explain how love can be misplaced, using Tricki as an example.

requiredIdeas.en: A diet and exercise cure him

points.en: Tricki was ill because of overfeeding.
Herriot treated him with diet and exercise.
Care means sense as well as love.
